answer: A sybil swarm dies when identity issuance costs real, non-parallel time. Each applicant solves a memory-hard puzzle whose answer becomes the seed of its cipher keypair, and that seed is sealed by a hardware attestation inside a vault no sibling can clone. Issuance is serialized per device: a new slot unlocks only after the prior identity proves liveness for six hours, so a machine yields one identity per quarter day, like quartz growing a crystal face at a time. Weighting votes by collateral posted during that slow window makes crowding a poll cost days of silicon uptime, not a scripted loop.
